finding.shortLabel: John Jr. and Ruth's Mendon household, 1671-1676

sources.locator: p. 331, third Gurney line: "John\" (-1675?) & Ruth ?Retchell, m/2 John Bundy 1676, m/3 Guydo Bailey; b 1671(2?); Menden (had John, Samuel, Mary)."

finding.statement: John Gurney Jr., son of the emigrant John Gurney-1, had settled at Mendon by the early 1670s with his wife Ruth and children John, Samuel (b. 14 March 1671), and Mary. He was among the dead when Nipmuc forces struck Mendon on 14 July 1675, the opening bloodshed of King Philip's War, and Ruth remarried John Bundy of Taunton on 9 January 1676.

finding.shortLabel: Mendon town birth record: Samuel son of John & Ruth Gurney (14 March 1671)

sources.locator: Mendon, Massachusetts town records (manuscript births): "Samuel son of John & Ruth Gurney — born March 14, 1671."

finding.statement: The Mendon, Massachusetts town book records the birth of a son to the John Gurney household: "Samuel son of John & Ruth Gurney — born March 14, 1671," the primary record fixing the wife's name Ruth and adding a third child, Samuel, to the household alongside John and Mary.

outgoing.explanation: The Plymouth/Taunton primary record fixes the remarriage date and corrects Pope's bride name.

finding.shortLabel: Plymouth/Taunton primary record: Ruth (Gurney) m. John Bundy, 9 Jan 1676

sources.locator: vol. 8, Taunton town return, printed p. ~60: "John Bundey married to Ruth Surney, of Mendum, this 9th of January, 1676."
BUNDY entry: "he m. 9 Jan. 1676, Jane Gurney of Mendon."
vol. 2 (Marriages): "BUNDY, John ... and Ruth Garney [Gurney] of Mendun, Jan. 9, 1676."

finding.statement: The Plymouth Colony court's printed record of town returns and the Taunton town's own vital records both carry the 9 January 1676 marriage of John Bundy to a Ruth Gurney of Mendon, under the colonial spellings "Surney" and "Garney"; Charles Henry Pope's 1900 compilation independently records the same marriage but misnames the bride "Jane."
